# Composer keyboard avoidance

The [keyboard focus/closing tracker](https://github.com/emilkowalski/vaul/blob/3e97aac6a38e4481bade71d7233ed6002e80f9b0/src/index.tsx#L476-L534) in `../../composer-keyboard-viewport.js` is adapted from Vaul at commit `3e97aac6a38e4481bade71d7233ed6002e80f9b0`, checked on 2026-10-29. The upstream MIT license is preserved in `LICENSE.md`. React, Radix, drawer gestures and modal semantics are not included.

Ordinary mobile reading uses the document. While the chat keyboard is detected, only the transcript becomes a native scrollport sized to the visual viewport; its gestures never write the root scroll position. The page, body and application shell remain in normal flow. A placeholder preserves the real document extent, preventing root scroll clamping on entry. The shared reading anchor transfers once on entry and once on exit, and the message window switches its observer root with it. The composer follows the measured keyboard rectangle and returns to its native bottom edge on dismissal, even if the textarea retains focus.

Composer lift compares client rectangles in one coordinate space. The document root's client top converts `visualViewport.pageTop + height` into that space; `offsetTop + height` alone is not a client coordinate on all Safari versions ([WebKit bug 306779](https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=306779)). On a short conversation, native focus panning can leave a large visual/layout offset; subtracting that offset again would lower the composer behind the keyboard after its initial correct position. Viewport events update the dock; native transcript scroll events do not reposition it.

The keyboard scrollport reserves only the measured composer height and external gap; the keyboard is already outside its height and needs no additional transcript padding or animated padding. Its range is the native `scrollHeight - clientHeight`. User drags and native momentum suppress anchor restoration. Bottom-follow is limited to readers already at the end when the keyboard scrollport shrinks or the composer grows.

The earlier document-only keyboard path still moved the composer and jumped the transcript on a physical iPhone after its callback guards were tightened. It simulated gestures and inertia by writing root `scrollTop`, leaving those writes coupled to Safari's focused-input viewport panning and native root insets ([WebKit bug 292603](https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=292603)). That gesture controller and its viewport-dependent range correction have been removed. Unlike the old whole-application keyboard frame, the current scrollport does not fix the body, clip an application ancestor, reverse message order, or remain active after keyboard closure.

Viewport events still depend on the browser: [WebKit bug 265578](https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=265578) documents late keyboard viewport reports. A bounded 350ms recheck handles late measurements; pinch zoom retains the current layout. Build and deployment checks do not establish keyboard behavior on a physical iPhone.
